chunks.text: There's another way we can build an ensemble of learners.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: We can build them using the same learning algorithm, but

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: train each learner on a different set of the data.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: This is what's called bootstrap aggregating or bagging.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: It was invented by Bremen in the late 80s, early 90s.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: Here's how bagging works.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: So what we do is we create a number of subsets of the data.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: I've drawn little bags here to represent bags of data.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: And each one of these is a subset of the original data.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: Now, how do we collect these?

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: Well, we do it randomly.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: So for this subset that contains n prime values,

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: and our original data set contains n different instances,

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: we grab n prime of them at random with replacement from this original data.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: So what with replacement means is, let's say we had, say, these values.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: We might grab this one and put it in our bag.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: We might randomly grab this one and put it in our bag.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: But each time we grab randomly,

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: we randomly choose across the whole collection of data.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: So we might choose this one again and put it in the bag.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: So this one and this one are really the same one, and they're repeated twice.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: And that's okay.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: That's what with replacement means.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: So we create altogether m of these groups or bags.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: And each one of them contains n prime different data instances chosen at random

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: with replacement.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: Let's note these things.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: So n is the number of training instances in our original data.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: n prime is the number of instances that we put in each bag.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: And m is the number of bags.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: We almost always want n prime to be less than n, usually about 60%.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: So each of these bags has about 60% as many training instances as our original data.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: But that's just a rule of thumb.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: Now we use each of these collections of data to train a different model.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: We have now m different models, each one trained on a little bit of different data.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: And just like when we have an ensemble of different learning algorithms,

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: here we have an ensemble of different models, we query in the same way.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: We query each model with the same x and we collect all of their outputs.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: We take the y output of each model, take their mean, and boom,

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: that's our y for the ensemble.

chunks.title: Bootstrap aggregating bagging
chunks.text: Now keep in mind, we can wrap this in a single API,
